title: Best Day Trips from Paklenica, Croatia 2027
metaDescription: Top day trips from Starigrad-Paklenica: Zadar, Nin, Krka, Plitvice, Kornati, Pag and Zrmanja rafting, with distances, drive times and euro prices.
content:
## Which Day Trips Work Best from Paklenica?

Starigrad-Paklenica sits on the Adriatic coast road (D8), at the foot of the Velebit mountains. Most day trips begin by driving south-west towards Zadar or by taking the Maslenica bridge and A1 motorway. That route gives access to two of Croatia's biggest national parks and to the northern Dalmatian islands.

The short list, by effort:

- **Easy and close:** Zadar, Nin, Pag island.
- **Full-day national parks:** Krka and Plitvice.
- **Active:** Zrmanja rafting, Kornati boat trip, Velebit jeep tours.

A rental car is the best way to do these. Public buses on the coast road (Zadar–Rijeka line) are infrequent and slow for park trips. The Zadar–Starigrad bus costs roughly €4–6 one way, but returns in the evening can be limited, so check the last departure before going.

## Zadar: The Closest City Trip (45 km)

Zadar is about 40 minutes by car from Starigrad-Paklenica. It is the main base for onward tours, and it works well alone as a half-day trip.

**Worth seeing:**
- The Roman Forum and the 9th-century Church of St. Donatus in the old town.
- The Sea Organ and Greeting to the Sun on the western waterfront. Both are free and best at sunset.
- The covered and open-air market near the old town walls, which has local cheese, fish and produce. It is busiest in the morning.

**Practical details:**
- Old-town parking is limited. Use the car parks outside the walls, which cost roughly €1–3 per hour depending on the zone.
- Zadar is also the place to catch a Kornati, Dugi Otok or island-hopping boat if you prefer a bigger operator.
- Summer afternoons are hot on the stone streets. Start at 9:00 and end with a late lunch.

## Nin: Salt Pans and Beaches (about 60 km)

Nin is a small, flat town on a lagoon, about 15 km north-west of Zadar. It is one of the oldest royal towns in Croatia. The historic centre sits on an islet joined to the land by stone bridges and can be walked in an hour.

Nin is also known for its salt pans, and the long Queen's Beach (Kraljičina plaža) has shallow water. This makes it a good choice for families with small children. Nin pairs well with Zadar on the same day, since the two are about 20 minutes apart.

## Krka National Park: Waterfalls and a Boat Ride (about 110 km)

Krka is roughly 1 hour 20 minutes from Paklenica by car, via the A1 motorway. It has several entrances. The Skradin entrance has a boat ride to Skradinski Buk, the largest waterfall, while Lozovac offers a bus to the same area. Roški Slap is a quieter option if the main falls are crowded.

**Costs and rules:**
- Entry varies by season, from about €20 in low season to about €40 in July and August. Check the official park site for the exact tariff before you go.
- Swimming at Skradinski Buk has been banned for years to protect the travertine. Do not plan a swim there.
- Allow 3–4 hours in the park, plus time in the nearby town of Skradin for lunch.

**Insider tip:** Arrive before 9:00 or after 15:00 in July and August. Tour buses arrive between 10:00 and 13:00 and the boardwalk becomes crowded.

**Combine with:** Šibenik, about 20 minutes from Skradin. Its UNESCO-listed St. James Cathedral is built entirely of stone, without wooden supports or binding material.

## Plitvice Lakes: The Longest Day, Worth It (about 150 km)

Plitvice is about 2 hours from Starigrad-Paklenica by road. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with 16 terraced lakes connected by waterfalls and wooden walkways.

**Costs and rules:**
- Entry is seasonal, from about €18 in winter and early spring to about €40 in summer. Day tickets are timed in peak season and often sell out, so book online in advance.
- Swimming is not allowed.
- Plan 4–6 hours on foot, using the park's electric boat and shuttle between sections.

**Opinion:** Plitvice is the one trip worth the 4-hour round-trip drive. It is more varied than Krka, and from Paklenica it is a better use of a full day than a second coastal stop. Visit in May, June or September–October. In July and August the walkways are often crowded, and in winter parts of the park can be icy or closed.

**Tip:** Drive in on the inland road through the Lika region rather than the coast, and stop for lunch at a roadside grill (roštilj) serving Lika lamb or cheese-filled štrukli.

## Kornati Islands: Boat Day Trip

Kornati National Park is an archipelago of about 89 islands, mostly bare limestone. Full-day boat trips run from the Zadar and Starigrad area between roughly May and October. Prices start at about €100 per adult, with lunch often included on smaller family-run boats and extra on larger ones. The park entry fee is usually included, but confirm when booking.

Boats usually stop for swimming and a viewpoint. Many include Telašćica Nature Park on Dugi Otok, which has sea cliffs and a salt lake (Mir). Trips can be cancelled in strong bora or jugo winds, so book a flexible-cancellation option and schedule it early in your stay.

## Zrmanja River: Rafting and Canyon Scenery (about 30–40 km)

The Zrmanja is a clear river that flows through a deep limestone canyon, with travertine waterfalls near Obrovac. Rafting, kayaking and canoeing run from spring to early autumn, and the best water levels are usually in spring. Group rafting costs about €50–80 per person depending on length and season. Operators generally pick up from Starigrad, and some include a swim.

Kayaking in the lower river, around Obrovac, is suitable for beginners. Water levels fall in late summer, so check with the operator beforehand.

## Pag Island: Cheese, Lamb and Moon-Like Landscape (45–75 km)

Pag is connected to the mainland by a bridge, about 45 km from Starigrad via the D8. The landscape is bare and rocky, with salt pans and olive and sage fields. The island is known for Paški sir, a hard sheep's-milk cheese, and for lamb.

- **Pag town** (about 75 km) has a lace-making tradition and a compact old centre.
- **Zrće beach**, near Novalja, is a party area with clubs; it is better skipped on a quiet family day.
- Buy cheese directly from a family producer or from the shops in Pag town. Prices are often around €30–45 per kilo for aged cheese.

## Velebit Mountain Tours and Back-Country Drives

Guided Land Rover and quad tours run into the Velebit uplands above the coast, with views over the Adriatic islands. They are best for those who want the mountain without long hiking. Typical prices are about €100–140 per adult for a half-day to 6–7-hour tour, depending on the operator. This differs from hiking in Paklenica itself, which is covered in a separate guide.

## How to Plan a Day Trip from Paklenica

- **Fuel and tolls:** The A1 motorway toll from the Maslenica junction to Šibenik is a few euros each way. Payment is by card or cash at the booth.
- **Start times:** Leave by 7:30–8:00 for Krka or Plitvice to arrive before the tour buses.
- **Weather:** Check the bora forecast. Strong wind can close the Maslenica bridge to some vehicles, and ferries and boats can be cancelled.
- **Cash:** Small konobas and family producers in rural areas often prefer cash.
- **Booking:** Plitvice tickets in summer and Kornati boats should be reserved a few days ahead. Zadar, Nin and Pag need no booking.

## Suggested Combinations

- **Two-in-one, easy:** Zadar plus Nin (about 20 minutes apart).
- **Nature day:** Krka plus Šibenik.
- **Slow day:** Pag bridge, cheese tasting, then a swim on the way back.
- **Adventure day:** Morning Zrmanja rafting, then dinner in Starigrad.

Prices on this page are approximate, and park tariffs, boat prices and bus timetables change from year to year. Confirm them with the park or operator before booking.

faq.question: What is the best day trip from Paklenica?
faq.answer: For a full day, Plitvice Lakes is the top choice, about 2 hours away. For an easier day, Zadar is 45 km and 40 minutes by car. Krka is the better option if you want waterfalls and a shorter drive.

faq.question: Can you visit Plitvice Lakes as a day trip from Paklenica?
faq.answer: Yes. The drive is about 150 km, or roughly 2 hours each way. Leave by 7:30 and book timed tickets online in summer, when the entry fee is up to about €40.

faq.question: Is Krka or Plitvice better from Starigrad-Paklenica?
faq.answer: Krka is closer (about 1 hour 20 minutes) and can be combined with Šibenik in one day. Plitvice is larger and more varied but requires a longer drive. Choose Krka for a relaxed day and Plitvice if you have only one national park to visit.

faq.question: Can you swim at Krka or Plitvice?
faq.answer: No. Swimming is banned at Plitvice, and at the main Skradinski Buk falls in Krka. For swimming, choose the Zrmanja river, Pag beaches or a Kornati boat trip.

faq.question: Do you need a car for day trips from Paklenica?
faq.answer: A car makes most trips far easier, especially Krka, Plitvice and Pag. Zadar can be reached by bus for about €4–6 one way, but check the return timetable. Rafting and boat operators usually offer pickup from Starigrad.

faq.question: How much does a Kornati boat trip cost?
faq.answer: Full-day trips start at about €100 per adult. Lunch is included on some smaller boats and extra on others, and the park fee may or may not be included. Book with free cancellation because wind can cancel trips.

faq.question: What is the best time of year for day trips from Paklenica?
faq.answer: May, June, September and early October offer the best balance of weather, crowds and prices. July and August are hot and busy, with the highest park fees. Boat trips and rafting generally run from spring to autumn.

quickAnswer: The best day trips from Paklenica are Zadar (45 km, 40 minutes), Krka National Park (about 110 km), Plitvice Lakes (about 150 km), the Kornati islands by boat, and Zrmanja river rafting near Obrovac. Zadar and Nin suit short trips. Plitvice and Krka need a full day and an early start.
